column5: what_evidence_would_settle_it
column6: notes

column5: whether both hands fully released the bottle and then re-established contact before pulling it closer
column6: Confirmed: complete hand-object release followed by re-contact is treated as a clear transition.

column5: whether both hands keep withdrawing after the candidate and leave a hand-free interval over the sink
column6: Both hands stop the manipulation and leave the sink interaction immediately after the candidate.

column5: whether the box is moved aside and released before the hands begin handling the exposed sachets
column6: The box-opening phase turns into handling the exposed contents, but the transition unfolds over several frames rather than one instant.

column5: the repeated left-right hand trajectory on both sides of the centre with no sustained stop
column6: The centre is one reversal within a regular back-and-forth cycle.

column5: whether both hands enter after the sustained hand-free interval and begin a new directed reach into the sink
column6: A sustained idle interval ends when both hands re-enter and initiate a new interaction.

column5: whether both hands fully release the cable and remain off it before later re-contacting it to begin winding
column6: Clear action-to-idle transition: both hands leave the cable before the next interaction begins.

column5: whether the same short tucking and smoothing motion repeats around the bowl without a sustained stop or hand withdrawal
column6: Continuous repetitive tucking around the bowl with no interaction reset.

column5: whether the hands maintain continuous contact with the same bowl and plastic wrap while continuing to position and smooth it
column6: The bowl entering the centre is part of the same wrapping task; there is no release or interaction reset.

column5: whether the right hand stops manipulating the strainer and makes contact with the faucet control
column6: The right hand switches interaction target from the strainer to the faucet while the left hand holds the strainer.

column5: whether both hands continue the same alternating pinching and folding rhythm across the centre without a sustained stop
column6: Continuous repetitive manipulation with no release or trajectory reset.

column5: whether the right hand sets aside the first component and picks a different pen body before joining it to the left-hand tip assembly
column6: A visible object swap and renewed contact separate the two assembly steps.

column5: whether both hands maintain the same repeated folding and flattening rhythm through the centre
column6: No interaction reset; this is internal motion within continuous folding.

column5: whether one hand remains on the tape-measure body while the other immediately repositions on the same tool after retraction
column6: The tape finishes retracting, but the tool remains continuously held; the other hand only repositions within the same operation.

column5: whether the right hand's sweeping rhythm continues across the centre while the other hand only repositions
column6: Brief repositioning is boundary-like, but the sweeping action appears continuous.

column5: a lower and wider view showing the hands, broom and dustpan as they move to the next floor section
column6: The critical interaction occurs at the bottom edge or off-screen.

column5: a lower view showing the hand or tool contacting the waste and the disposal target at the candidate time
column6: The critical interaction is outside the lower frame; only a partial pole and viewpoint change are visible.

column5: the same sweeping stroke repeating through the centre without a pause or trajectory reset
column6: Continuous repeated sweeping into the same dustpan.

column5: whether both hands fully release the small metal tin, leave a hand-free interval, and later re-contact it to place it back
column6: The tin interaction is fully reset: release and hand withdrawal are followed by a separate re-contact.

column5: whether both hands continue withdrawing from the sink immediately after the candidate instead of resuming the same motion
column6: Both hands stop manipulating the strainer and leave the interaction within about 0.4 seconds: a clear action-to-idle transition.

column5: whether the right hand leaves the closed box before both hands begin handling the loose material on the table
column6: Contact with the box ends and the hands move to a different interaction target.

column5: whether the fold-unfold hand cycle continues through the centre without a pause or new reach
column6: The same small folding cycle continues on both sides of the candidate.

column5: whether the strainer changes from being held near the faucet to making stable contact with the drain
column6: The strainer is transferred from the rinsing position and seated in the drain, creating a clear interaction-state change.

column5: whether both hands enter after the sustained hand-free interval and begin a coordinated reach toward the box
column6: A clear idle-to-action transition occurs when both hands re-enter and initiate a new reach.

column5: whether both hands release and leave the sponge before reaching toward the bowl
column6: The sponge is set down and contact ends before the next object interaction.

column5: whether both hands release the seated strainer and remain separated from it after the candidate
column6: Both hands terminate contact with the strainer and move apart, providing a visible interaction reset.

column5: whether the first package is set down and fully released before the hands reach for the different package
column6: The first object is released and the next reach targets a different package: a clear object-interaction reset.

column5: whether both hands maintain contact with the same remote while rotating it from one face or edge to another
column6: The object is continuously held; turning it is part of one inspection action.

column5: whether the right hand fully releases the bottle at the centre and remains off it before the later reach
column6: The bottle-move phase ends with a clear release and pause.

column5: whether the right hand leaves the strainer and establishes contact with the faucet control
column6: A clear interaction-target switch occurs from the strainer to the faucet control.

column5: whether the hands remain on the same tissue sheet while changing from flattening it to pinching and folding its edge
column6: Same object and continuous goal; the posture change is internal motion.

column5: whether both hands release the bottle and remain off it before re-contacting it to move it back
column6: A clear release and pause separates the two opposite-direction moves.

column5: whether both hands leave the wet plastic piece and bowl before reaching toward the plastic-wrap roll
column6: The wetting/crumpling interaction ends with hand withdrawal, followed by a new reach to the roll.

column5: whether the right hand leaves the pan rim and switches to the bottle or cap as the bottle is moved over the pan
column6: The interaction target changes from holding the pan to preparing and applying liquid from the bottle.

column5: whether both hands remain absent through the viewpoint shift and then re-enter in a new directed reach
column6: Despite the camera movement, the hand-free interval followed by a new reach makes the interaction reset visible.

column5: whether the tissue fully separates from the pack before both hands leave the pack and move toward the table
column6: Extraction completes, contact with the pack ends, and the hands move away to begin the next interaction.

column5: a forward-facing view showing the hands and camera while the wearable camera is being repositioned
column6: The camera faces a wall and the critical hand action is not visible.
